rows.grounds: locative of present passive participle from ā-han; denotes the state in which striking occurs
ablative used adverbially to express intensity or force of the action
compound para-tarpaṇa-hetu with ablative suffix -tas indicating reason or causal ground

items.question: Why does vehement striking function as the ground for supreme satisfaction?
premises: A state of being struck is present.
This striking serves as the cause of supreme satisfaction.
items.inference: Vehement striking is identified as the causal basis for supreme satisfaction.
uncertainties: The subject undergoing the striking is not explicitly named in this verse and relies on context.
items.plain_english: When being struck vehemently, it is so because this serves as the cause of supreme satisfaction.
